title: Development of VP30-targeted nanoparticles using DPS4 fusion peptides for the inhibition of Ebola virus.
authors: Wu, Fang; Huang, Yuanwei; Li, Rui; Gao, Peixuan; Lv, Pinpin; Wu, Guanxian; Ma, Yanhong; Ding, Qiang; Zhong, Jin; Su, Jiyan; Xu, Wei
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过DPS4融合肽纳米颗粒靶向埃博拉病毒VP30蛋白，利用晶体结构和MD模拟解析肽-VP30结合机制，但对象为病毒蛋白-肽互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，方法可迁移性有限。
abstract: Multiple outbreaks of Ebola virus in West Africa have posed significant threats to global public health owing to its high pathogenicity and fatality rates. Current treatments for Ebola Virus Disease are limited, underscoring the imperative for novel antiviral therapies. VP30, a critical RNA synthesis factor, interacts with nucleoprotein (NP) to facilitate Ebola viral genome transcription and replication. Notably, the host ubiquitin-ligase retinoblastoma-binding protein 6 (RBBP6) binds to VP30 at the same interface as NP, thereby inhibiting VP30-NP interactions and indicating that targeting this interface could advance antiviral drug development. In this study, we engineered six peptide mutants through amino acid substitutions at key VP30 binding sites. These mutants were fused to DNA-binding protein from starved cells 4 (DPS4) to assemble nanoparticles, enabling surface display of the peptides. Antiviral effects were evaluated using minigenome and transcription and replication-competent virus-like particles (trVLPs) systems. Among the variants, RPL1 and NPL3 peptides exhibited relatively strong apparent affinities with the VP30 and potent antiviral activity by disrupting Ebola viral genome transcription and replication. To elucidate the binding details between the peptides and VP30, we determined crystal structures of complexes between RPL1 or NPL3 peptides and VP30 via X-ray crystallography. Concurrently, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed the dynamic binding processes of these peptides to VP30. Structural analyses confirmed that the peptides bind to the VP30/NP interface and compete with NP. Our findings demonstrate that DPS4-fusion peptides effectively deliver peptides into cells as nanoparticles and inhibit VP30-NP interactions, presenting a novel antiviral strategy for Ebola virus.
abstract_zh: 西非地区多次爆发的埃博拉病毒因其高致病性和高致死率，对全球公共卫生构成了重大威胁。目前针对埃博拉病毒病的治疗手段有限，凸显了开发新型抗病毒疗法的紧迫性。VP30作为一种关键的RNA合成因子，与核蛋白（NP）相互作用，促进埃博拉病毒基因组的转录和复制。值得注意的是，宿主泛素连接酶视网膜母细胞瘤结合蛋白6（RBBP6）在NP相同的界面上与VP30结合，从而抑制VP30-NP相互作用，表明靶向该界面可能推动抗病毒药物的开发。在本研究中，我们通过在VP30关键结合位点进行氨基酸替换，设计了六种肽突变体。这些突变体与饥饿细胞DNA结合蛋白4（DPS4）融合，组装成纳米颗粒，实现肽的表面展示。使用小基因组和转录复制能力病毒样颗粒（trVLPs）系统评估抗病毒效果。在变体中，RPL1和NPL3肽表现出相对较强的与VP30的表观亲和力，并通过干扰埃博拉病毒基因组转录和复制展现出有效的抗病毒活性。为阐明肽与VP30之间的结合细节，我们通过X射线晶体学解析了RPL1或NPL3肽与VP30复合物的晶体结构。同时，分子动力学（molecular dynamics）模拟揭示了这些肽与VP30的动态结合过程。结构分析证实，这些肽结合于VP30/NP界面，并与NP竞争。我们的研究结果表明，DPS4融合肽作为纳米颗粒能有效将肽递送入细胞，并抑制VP30-NP相互作用，为埃博拉病毒提供了一种新型抗病毒策略。
